abstract: <jats:title>Abstract</jats:title><jats:p>Quantitative trait loci (<jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">QTL</jats:styled-content>s) for salt tolerance with additive, epistatic and <jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">QTL</jats:styled-content> × treatment interaction effects at seedling stage in wheat were identified. A set of 131 recombinant inbred lines derived from cross Chuan 35050 × Shannong 483 were evaluated under salt stress and normal conditions. Wide variation was found for all studied traits. A total of 18 additive and 16 epistatic <jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">QTL</jats:styled-content>s were detected, among which five and 11 were with significant <jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">QTL</jats:styled-content> × treatment effects. Ten <jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">QTL</jats:styled-content> clusters were identified, and each may represent a single gene or closely linked genes. The locus controlling shoot K<jats:sup>+</jats:sup>/Na<jats:sup>+</jats:sup> concentration ratio and shoot Na<jats:sup>+</jats:sup> concentration on chromosome 5A may be identical to <jats:italic>Nax2</jats:italic>. The interval <jats:italic>Xgwm6‐Xgwm538</jats:italic> on chromosome 4B for total dry weight was also identified in a previous study, both near the marker <jats:italic>Xgwm6</jats:italic>. The marker <jats:italic>Xgwm6</jats:italic> may be useful for marker‐assisted selection. Six pairs of homoeologous <jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">QTL</jats:styled-content>s were detected, showing synteny among the A, B and D genomes. These results facilitate understanding the mechanisms and the genetic basis of salt tolerance in wheat.</jats:p>
title: Mapping <scp>QTL</scp>s for salt tolerance with additive, epistatic and <scp>QTL</scp> × treatment interaction effects at seedling stage in wheat
